questions.question: What are the most effective safety restraints in a traffic crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash. Airbags work best when used with safety belts and protect you in front-end crashes. You should always wear both shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: You see a pedestrian crossing your lane where there is no crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing your lane, even if there is no crosswalk. Give them the right-of-way and wait until they have finished crossing.

questions.question: A driver's ability to drive can be impaired by:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe driving depends on being in good physical condition. Alcohol, medications, and being tired can all affect your ability to drive.

questions.question: Which of these is unlawful?

options.text: Passing another vehicle in a marked no passing zone.
Passing another vehicle over a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to pass in no passing zones, on hills, in curves, or where you cannot see far ahead. You cannot pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, or in work zones.

questions.question: You miss your exit on an interstate. What should you do?

options.text: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Speeding, not paying attention, and following too closely are major causes of crashes. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn and maintain your speed.
Speed up to clear the area quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians near the road. Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: As your blood alcohol level (BAC) increases, you become:
questions.correctAnswerText: More intoxicated.
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the amount of alcohol in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: An officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light. What should drivers do?

options.text: Follow the directions shown by the traffic light.
Follow the directions given by the officer.
Check what the cars next to them are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the officer.
questions.explanation: When an officer is directing traffic, follow their directions instead of the traffic light signals.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (in this case, 13 feet 6 inches).

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Time is the only way to lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or make you sober. They might help you stay awake, but they do not reduce alcohol from your body.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go and stay calm.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off to get back at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go and stay calm.
questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Ignore the behavior and keep driving safely. This prevents road rage situations.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a crosswalk. Watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either.
It harms driving skills but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it hard to see clearly. It also affects your judgment about speed and distance, makes you more reckless, and increases your chances of taking dangerous risks.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Slick roads are especially dangerous in turns and curves. Slow down more than you normally would when turning on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: A driving distraction is:

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. Distracted driving can cause accidents, injuries, and death.

questions.question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:

options.text: Always understand the risks they are taking.
Cannot fully control their body, mind, or vehicle.
Drive better because they are more careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot fully control their body, mind, or vehicle.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your judgment, vision, thinking, and reaction time. It is never safe to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When you change lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal before you start the lane change.
Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal for a few seconds before changing lanes. Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Make sure the lane is clear before you move.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. You should:

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of them.
Stop and let them cross safely.
Drive close to them to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing against the red light. Be careful around pedestrians in all situations.

questions.question: Mixing alcohol with drugs can:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can make both more dangerous. Never drive after drinking alcohol or taking drugs, and especially not after using both together.

questions.question: What is the only medically proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your system quickly but leaves slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower your blood alcohol content (BAC). The only way to lower your BAC is to wait for your body to process the alcohol.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can hurt your driving. If you are worried, excited, scared, angry, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress reduces your focus on driving. It is better to wait to drive than to risk driving when you are emotionally upset.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, go to the next rest stop or service area. Take a nap, stretch, or let someone else drive. Caffeine pills or energy drinks are not a safe substitute for rest and may make your driving more dangerous.

questions.question: On a freeway, if you miss your turn or exit, you should:

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane.
Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or place where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or place where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Instead, continue to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a shoulder or freeway is illegal.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even when no other cars are near.
Signal only if other cars are visible.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even when no other cars are near.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you change lanes, turn, or pull away from the curb. Do not skip signaling just because no other cars are visible. Make signaling a habit.

questions.question: You are required to stop your vehicle:

options.text: When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop your vehicle at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: A "No passing zone" sign tells drivers:

options.text: That it is not safe to pass.
To drive at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass other vehicles in that area. These signs are placed where visibility is limited and passing would be unsafe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn yield on green.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that when turning left on a green light, they must yield to oncoming traffic. You can complete your turn when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and yield to trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to trains.
questions.explanation: This round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. It tells drivers to slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.
